title: Reviewing a rail depot's overrides

blocks.text: A rail depot plans its maintenance jobs for the coming years, and the depot managers send manual overrides before every solve. Each override is a tuple: `("lock", job, year)` (the job starts in `year`) or `("ban", job)` (the job is not done). Each `Job` has the years it may start in, the crew that does it, and optionally a job it must follow, with a lag: it may start no earlier than `lag` years after that job starts.
The planning model has rules the overrides can contradict:

items: A job starts only in one of its own `years`.
A crew can start at most one job per year.
A job that follows another starts at least `lag` years after it.

blocks.text: Write `conflicts(jobs, overrides)` in `review.py`. It returns the set of job ids that take part in a conflict between the overrides and these rules, read from the overrides alone:

items: a job locked into a year that is not one of its `years`;
a job that is both locked and banned;
two or more jobs of one crew locked into the same year (all of them are reported);
a job locked into a year less than `lag` years after the year its predecessor is locked into (the follower is reported).

blocks.text: `jobs` maps each id to a `Job`. A job appears in at most one lock. List the cases on a sheet first, with the test instance's jobs, and decide which comparisons each needs. About fifteen lines.

cases.says: a list of overrides that agree with every rule reports nothing
a lock in a year the job may not start in is reported
a job both locked and banned is reported
two jobs of one crew locked into the same year are both reported
a job locked too soon after the job it follows is reported
two jobs of one crew locked into different years are not reported
a job locked exactly the lag after the job it follows is not reported

origin.section: A Conflicting Override Makes the Model Infeasible, or Quietly Changes It

concepts: overrides are checked against windows and rules before the solve
